author: Bhaskar Srinivasan <bhaskar.cmu@gmail.com> Sun Oct 25 22:53:52 2026 +0000
committer: Bhaskar Srinivasan Sun Oct 25 22:53:52 2026 +0000
sig: N 

fix(devcontainer): never start a second watcher; let FHIR stay stopped

archive-watcher.sh deleted watcher.lock unconditionally, assuming it was
the only launcher. With three launch points (postStart, postAttach, every
terminal), a supervisor killed while its watcher survived would let the
next one delete a live lock and run a second watcher (plus autostart's
sync) on the same worktree. It now waits while the lock names a running
archive_ai process and takes over when it exits; dead or reused PIDs are
still treated as stale.

post-start.sh restarted FHIR from every new terminal, even after a
deliberate `docker compose down`. Creating /workspaces/.no-fhir-autostart
now opts out. SETUP_LOG overrides the log path (for tests).

Tested in isolation (scratch repo, stub watcher): live lock -> waits, then
takes over; dead PID and reused non-archive PID -> starts at once; FHIR
opt-out honoured; no watcher without GITHUB_TOKEN; no-op outside Codespaces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>


diff --git a/.devcontainer/scripts/archive-watcher.sh b/.devcontainer/scripts/archive-watcher.sh
index 7e41636b..dd3b0290 100755
--- a/.devcontainer/scripts/archive-watcher.sh
+++ b/.devcontainer/scripts/archive-watcher.sh
@@ -12,11 +12,24 @@ LOCK_DIR="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}"
 exec 9> "$LOCK_DIR/archive-watcher-supervisor.lock"
 flock -w 5 9 || exit 0
 
-# This supervisor is the only launcher, so any watcher.lock left over from before
-# a restart is stale (and its PID may since have been reused by another process).
-rm -f "$ARCHIVE/ai-chat-documentation/logs/watcher.lock"
+WATCHER_LOCK="$ARCHIVE/ai-chat-documentation/logs/watcher.lock"
+
+# True if watcher.lock names a running archive_ai process. A supervisor can be
+# killed while its watcher survives; starting another beside it (autostart.sh
+# also runs a sync) would put two processes on one git worktree at once.
+watcher_alive() {
+  local pid
+  pid=$(head -1 "$WATCHER_LOCK" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+  [ -n "$pid" ] && grep -qa archive_ai "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null
+}
 
 while true; do
+  if watcher_alive; then
+    sleep "$RETRY_SECONDS"
+    continue
+  fi
+  # Any lock left now is stale (its PID may since have been reused).
+  rm -f "$WATCHER_LOCK"
   if [ ! -e "$ARCHIVE/.git" ]; then
     git -C "$REPO" worktree prune
     if ! { git -C "$REPO" fetch -q origin ai-chat-history \
diff --git a/.devcontainer/scripts/post-start.sh b/.devcontainer/scripts/post-start.sh
index 36a429fa..49bc63c4 100755
--- a/.devcontainer/scripts/post-start.sh
+++ b/.devcontainer/scripts/post-start.sh
@@ -9,17 +9,21 @@
 # the lifecycle commands can be killed when the command returns, so the later
 # runs restart whatever did not survive; when everything is up this is a no-op.
 #
+# To keep FHIR stopped (e.g. after `docker compose down`), create
+# /workspaces/.no-fhir-autostart; delete it to resume auto-start.
+#
 # Codespaces only: Ona runs its own fhirServer / aiChatArchiveWatcher services
 # (.ona/automations.yaml), and a second watcher there would fight the first.
 [ "${CODESPACES:-}" = "true" ] || exit 0
-LOG=/workspaces/setup.log
+LOG="${SETUP_LOG:-/workspaces/setup.log}"
 SCRIPTS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
 REPO="$(cd "$SCRIPTS/../.." && pwd)"
 TAG="post-start(${1:-manual})"
 mkdir -p "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-/workspaces/.claude-home}"
 
 # FHIR server (H2, in-memory). docker-in-docker's daemon may still be starting.
-if [ -z "$(docker ps -q --filter name=fhir-agent-fhir --filter status=running 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+if [ ! -e /workspaces/.no-fhir-autostart ] \
+   && [ -z "$(docker ps -q --filter name=fhir-agent-fhir --filter status=running 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[$TAG] $(date -u +%FT%TZ) FHIR: starting" >> "$LOG"
   setsid nohup bash -c "
     for i in \$(seq 1 60); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done

## The guides

**[Demo guide](./demo-guide.md)** — how to experience the system, and how to demo it to four
audiences (clinician, insurer, architect/developer, layperson). Includes the prep checklist that
stops a demo failing in front of people: the FHIR server is in-memory and adjudication fails
closed, so you must seed first.

**[Developer guide](./developer-guide.md)** — the mental model, the lifecycle of one claim
through the packages, the invariants you must not break, the local dev loop, a list of traps that
have already cost real hours, and how to add a rule / a downstream call / a FHIR artefact.

**[Testing guide](./testing-guide.md)** — what is tested (with counts), what is *not* (with
honesty), how to run every level, and how to write unit / white-box / component / interface /
e2e tests here. Its case study — how a dead clinical-safety check passed every test for several
milestones — is the most useful thing in this folder.

**[Gateway runbook](./gateway-runbook.md)** — the single operational source of truth for the Kong
edge across Phases 1 and 2 (later phases add no edge routes): why two gateways exist, which one owns which route in each strangler
state (S0/S1/S2), exact local procedures (including the template→generated config flow), the
cloud position, the migration and its rollback, and troubleshooting.

## Design and decisions

**[`phase2/`](./phase2/README.md)** — the claims-adjudication modernisation slice.

- **[`decisions.md`](./phase2/decisions.md)** — the ADR-style index of every architectural
  decision (D1–D8, C1–C5, plus later ones) with **status and supersession markers**, linking to
  where each rationale lives. Start here to audit *what was decided and whether it still holds*.

- **[`requirements.md`](./phase2/requirements.md)** — normative. Requirements R1–R19, including
  the Decision Contract (R17), audit invariants and idempotency (R18), and the test matrix (R19).
  What we agreed to build, and deviations from the source PRD. No implementation detail, no
  status, no commit history.
- **[`plan.md`](./phase2/plan.md)** — architecture, service topology, gateway and local/cloud
  parity, cloud design, milestones, engineering standards, and **§16 future work**.
- **[`source-prd.md`](./phase2/source-prd.md)** — the archived DRAFT PRD that seeded the work.
  The *input*, not the contract; kept for provenance.

**[`phase3/`](./phase3/README.md)** — Provider Search & Referral. M1–M7 complete; Phase 3b
(live cloud deployment) not started.

- **[`README.md`](./phase3/README.md)** — the canonical status statement for Phase 3. Start
  here; other Phase 3 documents link to it rather than restating status.
- **[`prd.md`](./phase3/prd.md)** — problem, goals/non-goals, requirements, success metrics.
- **[`design.md`](./phase3/design.md)** — architecture, both agents' tool contracts, the

## 2. Running the tests

**Everything that needs no stack** (the fast loop — run this before every commit):

```bash
# Python — all suites (config in pytest.ini)
pytest

pytest agent-platform/tests -q               # separate invocation (see pytest.ini's comment)

# Java — the Phase 2 services and the Phase 4 emulator
mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test
mvn -f rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml test
mvn -f epic-emulator/pom.xml test
```

**A single level or suite:**

```bash

mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test -Dtest=RulesEngineTest        # one class
mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test -Dtest=HttpTriageClientTest   # the contract test
```

Several Phase 3 suites need a local Postgres (`docker compose --profile phase3 up -d postgres`,
then `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://provider_registry:‹redacted:url-credentials›localhost:5432/provider_registry`)
and self-skip — not error — when it's unreachable, same convention as the rest of this project.
`provider-search-agent`'s groundedness eval additionally self-skips without an Anthropic key,
since it makes real, billed API calls. The agent suites (`mcp-agent`, `outcome-prediction-agent`)
run against the free self-hosted model — `ollama serve` with `llama3.2:1b` pulled — and
self-skip their live tests without it.

**End-to-end** (needs the stack; self-skips if it is not up, so it is safe to collect anywhere):

```bash
docker compose --profile phase2 up --build -d
pytest e2e/
```

`e2e/conftest.py` seeds the FHIR fixtures itself — you do **not** need to run the demo seeder
first. `e2e/test_epic_emulator_acceptance.py` (Phase 4) needs `fhir-service`, `triage-service`
and `epic-emulator` running; `e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py` (Phase 8) brings up the
compose `phase8` profile itself and tears it down afterwards. This matters: the demo FHIR server is in-memory, so it boots empty every time.
